content.value_statement: Email teams need clear tests that isolate variables and avoid false winners. This skill plans email experiments and reads results with documented sample, power, and significance gates.
actual_capabilities: Chooses A/B, multivariate, send-time, or hold-out mode from the user request.
Builds a variant matrix that isolates one variable per cell.
Plans sample size, minimum detectable effect, duration, and power from stated baselines.
Defines primary, secondary, and guardrail metrics for email experiments.
Reads finished ESP exports and applies a documented significance gate.
Returns a promote, kill, or keep-testing decision in plain language.
limitations: It does not write email creative, subject lines, or CTA copy.
It does not connect to ESP APIs without separate user-provided tooling.
It uses documented calculations and table lookups, not live statistical software.
It depends on accurate baselines, list size, and exported result counts.

use_cases.title: Plan a Lifecycle Test
use_cases.description: Create a subject, CTA, or send-time test for a recurring lifecycle campaign.

use_cases.title: Read an Experiment Export
use_cases.description: Evaluate a completed ESP test and decide whether to promote, kill, or keep testing.

use_cases.title: Measure Incremental Revenue
use_cases.description: Design a randomized hold-out group for conversion or revenue-per-recipient lift.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Basic A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an A/B subject-line test. Baseline open rate is 38%, target lift is 3 points, and list size is 12,000.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Send-Time Testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a send-time test for a weekly newsletter. Baseline open rate is 40%, list size is 20,000, and the goal is retention.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multivariate Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a 2 by 2 subject and CTA experiment. Baseline click rate is 2.1%, daily send volume is 8,000, and target lift is 1 point.

prompt_templates.title: Read a Finished Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this finished ESP export and decide whether to promote, kill, or keep testing. Include sample, lift, p-value gate, and guardrails.

output_examples.input: A retention team asks for a subject-line A/B test with 38% baseline open rate and 12,000 recipients.
output: Mode: A/B subject test with control and one changed subject line.
Plan: detect a 3-point lift with documented per-cell sample and a fixed read date.
Decision rule: promote only if p is below 0.05 and guardrails stay stable.

output_examples.input: A newsletter owner wants to know the best hour to send a weekly campaign.
output: Mode: send-time test with subject, segment, and creative held constant.
Plan: split recipients across time arms and compare same-window engagement.
Guardrail: avoid confounding hour effects with day-of-week effects.

output_examples.input: An analyst provides delivered, opened, clicked, and converted counts for two variants.
output: Read-out: compare variant rates with a named significance method.
Interpretation: report observed lift against the minimum practical lift.
Call: promote, kill, or keep testing with the reason stated plainly.

best_practices: Provide baseline rate, list size, sendable recipients per day, and minimum worthwhile lift.
Change one variable per cell so the winner has a clear cause.
Set sample size and read date before launch, then avoid early winner calls.
anti_patterns: Changing subject, CTA, and creative in the same cell.
Promoting a variant from early results before the planned sample is complete.
Using open-rate lift for a hold-out that should measure conversion or revenue.

faq.question: Can this skill write the email copy under test?
faq.answer: No. It designs the experiment and reads results. Use a creative skill to write copy.

faq.question: Can it analyze an existing ESP export?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide delivered counts and outcome counts for each variant.

faq.question: Does it support send-time tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It holds content constant and compares engagement across planned send times.

faq.question: Does it support hold-out groups?
faq.answer: Yes. It can size and interpret randomized send versus no-send controls.

faq.question: What inputs are most important?
faq.answer: Baseline rate, list size, send volume, target lift, and final variant counts are most important.

faq.question: Can it call a winner early?
faq.answer: No. It warns against early calls before the planned sample and read date.
